A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

silylation of cellulose is possible at a low curing condition of 40 C, and that this silylation is not restricted only on the hydroxys but also on the carboxylate moiety of TEMPO-oxidised nanocelluloses.
the use of TEMPO-NC from OPEFB as a precursor for the synthesis of a new type of silylated celluloses is a novel approach and has been achieved for the first time.
the silylation of the TEMPO-oxidised nanocelluloses from OPEFB is possible at a lower curing temperature of 60 °C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of TEMPO-NC from OPEFB is a viable alternative to the expensive TEMPO-oxidation of cellulose from other sources.
the silylation reaction can be carried out at a lower curing temperature of 100 °C as compared in the literature.
silylation can be done at low temperature and the reaction is not limited to the hydroxyl groups of the cellulose, but also to the carboxylic moieties.
